report.body:
The operation began on the night of Wednesday 4 November 2026 after an anonymous
tip that a car was being used to sell drugs in Água Clara. The tip pointed
to a white VW Gol in the Jardim das Palmeiras neighbourhood. The driver
fled when Military Police approached the car and was caught after a chase of
several blocks. Officers found a portion of cocaine in the car. At the
driver's home they found more marijuana portions and a precision scale.

The driver, aged 30, was already known to the Civil Police's General
Investigations Section (SIG). Investigators identified a second address
used to store a larger quantity of drugs. There they found 59 tablets of
marijuana weighing about 54 kilograms. Two men aged 18 and 20 were arrested
in the act at that address. The investigation led officers to a third
suspect, aged 22, with whom they seized about 500 grams of marijuana and another
precision scale. A 28-year-old man already investigated for drug
trafficking and wanted on an open arrest warrant was also detained.

In all, five men were arrested. Four were booked in the act for drug
trafficking and association for trafficking, and the fifth was held under the
judicial warrant. Police put the operation's total at about 54.64 kilograms
of marijuana and cocaine together. Officers also seized a car, a
motorcycle, three precision scales, three mobile phones, packaging and about
R$250 in cash. The operation was a joint action by the Military Police and
the Civil Police. The men were taken to the Civil Police station in Água
Clara for legal procedures.

Military police in Mojuí dos Campos, in western Pará, arrested João Victor
Castro on the afternoon of Thursday 12 November 2026 after finding substances
resembling marijuana and cocaine. The approach took place at about 17:45 at
Travessa São Sebastião with Rua Joana D'Arc, in the town. G1 reported that
officers were patrolling the Cidade Alta 2 neighbourhood when the man grew
nervous at the sight of the police car, which prompted the stop. He was

drug trafficking in the region, after which the suspect confessed and said he

neighbourhood. There, according to the military police, they found 31
packets of material resembling cocaine and 12 packets of material resembling
marijuana. The house search also turned up R$301 in cash. Officers
further seized a loose portion of drug outside its packaging, packaging material
and a black Samsung A14 mobile phone.

marijuana and put the cash at R$300. The man was arrested for drug
trafficking, and he and the seized material were taken to the 16th Civil Police

report.body:
Officers of the Mossos d'Esquadra, Catalonia's police force, detained seven men
aged between 29 and 55 in an industrial warehouse in Cabanes, Alt Empordà, on 1
October 2026. The officers seized 8,025 kilograms of hashish in the
warehouse, the force said. The hashish was packed in large raffia sacks
filled with rubber crumb, a method the Mossos said is used to make it harder to
detect at police or customs checks. Inside, the officers found the seven
men unloading pallets from an articulated lorry's trailer and preparing to load
the hashish into several vans for distribution. Surveillance officers had
seen people replace the vehicles' original number plates with others fixed with
cable ties, apparently to hinder identification.

The Mossos valued the hashish at more than 16.2 million euros on the illegal
market. Officers also found a firearm in one of the detainees' vans.
The warehouse was an almost entirely open space with nothing to indicate
business or residential use, and police described it as a logistics base for
drug trafficking.

The investigation began in June 2026 with the interception of a van carrying
nearly 2,400 kilograms of hashish in Viladecans, in the Baix Llobregat, a case
taken by the criminal section of the Tribunal d'Instància of Gavà.
Surveillance of the warehouse showed people and vehicles visiting intermittently
with no business activity, and movements that looked like loading and unloading. The seven detainees were brought before the civil and investigating section
of the Tribunal d'Instància of Figueres. The investigation remains open and
the Mossos said further arrests or operations were not ruled out. The force
said the volume of hashish made the raid one of its most significant operations.

report.body:
Spain's UDYCO drug unit arrested a truck driver at the port of Ceuta carrying a
stash of hashish hidden in a sophisticated false bottom. Officers
intercepted the truck on the port road at the Muelle de Poniente and searched it
with support from the UPR prevention unit and the canine group. They found
the hashish and detained the driver, showing him the drugs found in the vehicle
he was driving.

The truck appeared empty and was heading toward boarding for Spain when a
specialist drugs dog alerted, prompting an exhaustive hours-long search inside
and outside the vehicle. After the hours-long detailed inspection, officers
found a large number of bags full of hashish inside the truck's structure.
Officers recovered numerous bags of hashish from the trailer's false bottom,
with first estimates putting the haul above 300 kilograms although police gave
no official weight. The submitted account describes the seizure as about
300 kilograms of hashish arriving from Morocco.

The handcuffed driver was taken to police headquarters and placed under
investigation for an offence against public health. The driver was brought before a judge on Sunday 15 November and ordered into pre-trial detention on charges of an offence against public health. Police link the
operation to open UDYCO investigations into groups moving hashish from Ceuta to
mainland Spain in heavy vehicles with hidden compartments. The investigation remains open, with suspicions of further shipments using hidden compartments in heavy vehicles.

report.body:
Officers of the National Police's Drugs and Organised Crime Unit (Udyco)
arrested at least three people on Mallorca who were storing almost 50 kilos of
hashish for sale. The operation ended with five arrests: four men and one woman. The suspects received the hashish from the Spanish
mainland in courier parcels, according to the newspaper's case sources. A parcel containing 24 kilos of hashish was addressed to a man living in Palma, who was identified and arrested after officers seized it. The
arrests took place on Wednesday 4 November. Officers searched a home in
Marratxí, a municipality east of Palma, and another in a town in es Raiguer, the
district around the town of Inca. An investigating court in Palma declared
the case secret. Investigators had followed the suspects for some time;
over the previous months they had collected parcels of the drug from courier
companies and kept them at home for sale through others in the network.

In the Marratxí search, police found a large quantity of hashish in a chest
freezer and an air rifle. At the main suspect's home officers found 36 kilos of hashish, an air rifle with a silencer and about 10,000 euros in cash. A woman was arrested there over her alleged link
to the criminal organisation and was released at the police station hours later. The National Police describe the man and the woman as the suspected perpetrators of drug trafficking and membership of a criminal group or organisation. Two more people were arrested the same day, and all the suspects are
Spanish nationals. A fifth person was arrested over links to the case. At a second home officers arrested a man described as the custodian and transporter of the drug and found two kilos of cocaine, prepared doses, cutting agent, a 9mm pistol with cartridges, a bow with arrows and a hydraulic press.

The investigation is still open, further arrests are not ruled out, and the
suspects were due to appear before a Palma court in the coming hours. Police said they had dismantled a drug-trafficking gang on Mallorca.

cases.title: 44 pieces of "Kush" seized in Thiaroye
cases.why: In West Africa "Kush" is the street name of a synthetic drug (synthetic cannabinoids, often with nitazene opioids), not a cannabis variety. The article names nothing else. The substance has to be identified from evidence, not from a trade name, and the tracker already holds real cannabis cases from the same suburb.

attempts.decision_title: Thiaroye Kao kush case falls outside cannabis scope
attempts.explanation: Seneweb reports that two men were arrested in Thiaroye Kao on 13 November 2026 by the research brigade of the Yeumbeul Sud police station, and that officers seized 44 pieces of kush, 3,000 CFA francs and a mobile phone; a second outlet gives the same figures. The tracker covers cannabis, and neither account identifies the product as cannabis: it is called only kush and narcotics. Senegalese reporting describes kush as a synthetic drug — SeneNews calls it a chemical mixture imitating the effects of cannabis, and an addiction specialist quoted by the national agency APS describes it as nitazene-type synthetic opioids, distinct from and more accessible than cannabis — so the product falls in the synthetic drugs excluded from this tracker. report.body:
Jandarma crime-investigation teams (JASAT) detained 17 suspects in simultaneous
raids on eight addresses in Mustafakemalpaşa, Bursa, on 11 November 2026. A
court jailed one of the 17, identified in reports only as H.F., and released the
other 16. The jailed suspect was taken to the Bursa E Type Closed Prison. Nine gendarmerie public-order teams, five JASAT teams, one gendarmerie
special operations team and two sniffer dogs took part in the raids.

Construction worker Mehmet Arıcan left his workplace in Taşpınar Mahallesi,
Mustafakemalpaşa, at about 12:30 on 7 September 2010 and was reported missing. His body was found four days later at Karanlıkdere, in woodland, where he
had been shot dead with a hunting rifle. Three suspects detained at the
time were not prosecuted and the file was placed under permanent search.

The Mustafakemalpaşa chief public prosecutor's office reopened the file,
re-examining phone (HTS) records, financial investigations and new witness
statements. Gendarmerie teams put 22 mobile phone lines belonging to 10
suspects under interception. Investigators also took a statement from a
person willing to testify in secret at the Mustafakemalpaşa prosecutor's office. Investigators established that Arıcan and H.F. had been at odds at the time
over Arıcan entering a cannabis (kenevir) field without permission. They
said they strongly suspected eight other people of helping the alleged killer
flee and hide. Justice Minister Akın Gürlek said the Bursa murder had been
solved and thanked the teams involved.

city of Mykolaiv, convicted a 51-year-old local resident of manufacturing and
storing narcotics for sale on an especially large scale and of illegally sowing
and growing cannabis. The court sentenced him to nine years' imprisonment. The verdict has not entered into legal force.

exposed the 51-year-old man's unlawful activity in July. During an
authorised search of his home officers found and seized more than 10 kilograms

the operation.
